title: Count Artifacts That Can Be Extracted
statement:
Some rectangular artifacts are buried in an `n x n` grid whose rows and columns are numbered from 0. Artifact `i` is `artifacts[i] = [r1, c1, r2, c2]`: it occupies every cell from its top-left corner `(r1, c1)` to its bottom-right corner `(r2, c2)`, inclusive.

Each entry `dig[j] = [r, c]` means you dig out cell `(r, c)`, exposing whatever lies there. An artifact can be extracted only when every cell it occupies has been dug. Return how many artifacts can be extracted.

The input guarantees that artifacts never share a cell, that each artifact covers at most 4 cells, and that no cell appears twice in `dig`.
constraints: Each artifact covers at most 4 cells
The entries of dig are unique
signature: int digArtifacts(int n, int[][] artifacts, int[][] dig)
notes:
## Intuition

For every artifact we must ask, cell by cell, "was this dug?". Scanning the whole `dig` list for each cell works but costs O(artifacts × dig). Since an artifact has at most 4 cells, the real cost is the lookup, so put every dug cell in a hash set first and each question becomes O(1).

## Approach

1. Encode each dug cell `(row, col)` as the single number `row * n + col` and add it to the set `dug`.
2. For each artifact `[r1, c1, r2, c2]`, assume it is `uncovered`.
3. Visit every cell of its rectangle; as soon as one is missing from `dug`, mark it not uncovered and stop scanning.
4. If the artifact stayed uncovered, add one to `count`.
5. Return `count`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 2`, so `dig = [[0,0],[0,1]]` becomes `dug = {0, 1}`. The first artifact `[0,0,0,0]` is only cell 0, which is dug, so `count = 1`. The second artifact `[0,1,1,1]` covers cells 1 and 3; cell 1 is dug but cell 3 (`(1,1)`) is not, so it stays buried. The answer is `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(D + A), with D dug cells and A artifacts: each artifact checks at most 4 cells.
- Space: O(D) for the set of dug cells.

## Pitfalls

- A key such as `row * n + col` must be unique per cell; `row + col` would mix up `(0,1)` and `(1,0)`.
- Both corners are inclusive, so loop with `<=` on rows and columns.
- Dug cells that hold no artifact do not count for anything; count artifacts, not dug cells.
- An artifact is extracted only when **all** its cells are dug; one missing cell is enough to fail it.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `dug` | set of dug cells, each encoded as `row * n + col` |
| `count` | number of artifacts fully dug out so far |
| `r1`, `c1`, `r2`, `c2` | corners of the current artifact |
| `uncovered` | whether every cell checked so far for this artifact was dug |
| `row`, `col` | the cell being checked |

narration.2: A hash set will answer "was this cell dug?" in constant time.
narration.3: Go through every dug cell once.
narration.4: Store the cell as one number, row * n + col, which is unique for each cell.

narration.8: Take each artifact by its two corners.
narration.9: Assume it is fully exposed until a buried cell shows up.
narration.10: Walk its rows, stopping early once a buried cell was found.
narration.11: Walk its columns; corners are inclusive.
narration.13: Then this artifact cannot be extracted...
narration.14: ...and there is no need to check its other cells.
narration.18: Every cell of the artifact was dug.
narration.22: Return how many artifacts were fully dug out.
